definitions.gloss: distrust; feeling of mistrust; sense of distrust
definitions.explanation: A feeling of not being able to trust someone or something. Often used in discussions about relationships, politics, or institutions.

examples.japanese: {不信感|ふしんかん}を{抱|いだ}く。
{政治|せいじ}に{対|たい}する{不信感|ふしんかん}が{広|ひろ}がっている。
{度重|たびかさ}なる{嘘|うそ}が{原因|げんいん}で、{彼|かれ}に{対|たい}する{不信感|ふしんかん}が{消|き}えなくなった。
examples.english: Due to repeated lies, my distrust toward him wouldn't go away.

notes:
FORMATION:
{不|ふ} (non-/un-) + {信|しん} (trust) + {感|かん} (feeling). Describes the subjective feeling or sense of distrust, rather than the objective state.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不信感|ふしんかん}を{抱|いだ}く (to harbor distrust)
- {不信感|ふしんかん}が{広|ひろ}がる (distrust spreads)
- {不信感|ふしんかん}を{持|も}つ (to hold distrust)
- {不信感|ふしんかん}が{募|つの}る (distrust grows)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不信|ふしん}: distrust — the state itself, without the {感|かん} (feeling) nuance
- {疑念|ぎねん}: doubt, suspicion — more intellectual than emotional
